subject: Runway contingency: fallback fee vs usage-smoothing credits
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@hedgeview.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lara Chen <lara@hedgeview.ai>, Hedgeview Procurement <procurement@hedgeview.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence — short runway and next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the sync this morning. We reviewed usage overnight and we’re running into a hard runway problem — we’re about to exhaust the allocated credits and a full extension feels heavy given our current spend cadence. Two quick asks: 1) can we extend the pilot by 3 weeks without redoing the whole addendum, and 2) is there an option other than buying token credits? Specifically, would Redwood consider a short-term "fallback fee" (flat fee to guarantee capacity for the window) instead of per-token top-up?

If a fallback fee is an option, what would it cover (throughput / latency / SLA), and what’s the delta vs converting to a reserved package? I attached our latest usage snapshot.

Appreciate a quick outline — procurement needs a baseline today so we can decide.

Attachments: current_pilot_usage_report.pdf (summary)

—Samir
Samir Rao
Head of ML Platform
Hedgeview Labs

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@hedgeview.ai>, Lara Chen <lara@hedgeview.ai>
Cc: Hedgeview Procurement <procurement@hedgeview.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Runway contingency: fallback fee vs usage-smoothing credits

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads up and for the usage report — helpful. High level we can do two straightforward paths for the next 3 weeks:

1) Credit top‑up (pay-as-you-go): immediate token top-up that layers onto your current pilot balance. No contract change, fastest to implement.

2) Short-term fallback fee (one-time flat fee for the 3-week window): we can price a fallback fee that guarantees a reserved pool for your pilots (throughput cap and soft-SLA). This prevents throttling and keeps latency targets intact. Fee covers capacity only (no change to data residency or long-term SLA).

3) Convert remaining runway into a short reserved commitment with a small conversion discount — this is effectively an early step toward Dedicated. This requires a short amendment.

I attached a draft term sheet for the fallback fee to give the team something concrete to react to. Recommendation: if procurement needs one number today, fallback fee is usually the quickest to approve and keeps your team from having to estimate token usage.

If you like, I’ll loop in Finance and Legal for exact numbers and a fast-turn amendment. What’s the preferred approval path — PO or signed addendum?

Attachments: fallback_fee_term_sheet.docx (term outline)

Best,

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Runway contingency: fallback fee vs usage-smoothing credits — pricing/legal check

David / Kim — forwarding Samir’s ask. Quick thoughts below; want your legal / pricing take so I can respond with numbers by EOD Friday.

Summary of options I told them:
- Top‑up credits (standard) — zero friction, higher per‑unit cost.
- Fallback fee (3 weeks) — flat fee that reserves capacity. Quick to approve, simpler procurement.
- Short reserved conversion — better unit economics but requires amendment.

Draft fallback structure I think will work:
- Fallback fee: $18,000 one‑time for 3 weeks, guarantees 4k concurrent token throughput cap and soft 250ms p99 latency objective.
- If Customer converts to a 3‑month reserved within 60 days, we rebate 25% of fallback fee toward the first invoice.
- Fallback fee does not change data handling or entitle to Dedicated SLAs.

Negotiation points: 1) rebate % (20–30%), 2) definition of "convert" trigger and proof of purchase, 3) language on overage (do we bill token overages on top of fallback?).

David — can you draft two short sentences for the amendment that capture the rebate and the overage rule?
Kim — is $18k reasonable vs historic pilot surge coverage? If not, what feels closer?

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Fwd: Runway contingency: fallback fee vs usage-smoothing credits — pricing/legal check

Marissa — happy to keep it tight. Two suggested lines for amendment and a redline note:

1) Rebate clause (suggested legal text): "If Customer executes a Reserved Capacity Order for Redwood Inference services within sixty (60) days following payment of the Fallback Fee, Redwood will credit twenty‑five percent (25%) of the Fallback Fee toward Customer's first Reserved Capacity invoice; such credit is non‑refundable and applies only once."

2) Overage language: "Fallback Fee provides a reserved capacity pool as described in the Term Sheet. Usage that exceeds the reserved capacity in any billing period will be billed at Customer's then‑current pay‑as‑you‑go rates and is not eligible for rebate credit."

Redline note: make sure the term "Reserved Capacity Order" is clearly defined to include minimum billing period and invoicing path — finance will want a PO or signed SOW to trigger the rebate.

Kim — pricing check — $18k feels on the high side relative to prior short surges for similar accounts; for a 3‑week window I would suggest $12k–$15k unless we are guaranteeing unusually high throughput. If we offer the 25% rebate, that further reduces our net to ~$9k–$11.25k effective.

—David

Redwood Inference

Subject: Final proposal: 3‑week runway — fallback fee + conversion rebate (options)

Hi Samir / Lara — thanks for the quick turnaround while you triage. Based on internal review here’s a clean, actionable set of options so procurement can choose today: 

Option A — Token top‑up (fastest):
- Incremental tokens (applied immediately) — Estimated cost: $9,400 for projected 3‑week usage (no contract change).

Option B — Fallback fee (recommended for predictability):
- One‑time fallback fee: $14,000 (covers a reserved throughput pool sized for current usage; soft p99 latency objective).
- If you execute a Reserved Capacity Order within 60 days, Redwood will credit 25% of the fallback fee ($3,500) toward your first reserved invoice.
- Overage beyond the reserved pool billed at standard pay‑as‑you‑go rates.

Option C — Short reserved conversion (best unit economics):
- Convert remaining pilot balance into a 3‑month reserved package with a conversion discount (requires signed amendment / PO). Finance can provide specific P&L impact on request.

Attachments: amendment_draft.pdf (proposed short addendum), term_sheet_fallback_signed_stub.pdf (fallback specifics)

If Procurement wants the quickest path: confirm Option B and whether you’ll need a PO or a signed addendum — we can either issue an invoice or send a DocuSign addendum (link below). If you prefer a numbers call, I can get David and Kimberly on a 20‑minute call tomorrow morning.

Thanks — let me know which option you want to move forward with and I’ll push the paperwork.
